newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish rapeseed output seen down in 1997 - minister. [CORRECTED 15:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Polish rapeseed output seen down in 1997 - minister. [CORRECTED 15:40 GMT]

text.p: Polish rapeseed output is seen falling to between 400,000 and 450,000 tonnes in 1997 from 500,000 tonnes in 1996, and meeting about 40 percent of the country's demand, the agriculture minister said on Monday.
Jaroslaw Kalinowski told Reuters in an interview that the government was mulling lowering duties on rapeseeds.
Kalinowski said the agriculture ministry wanted to introduce an import quota on rapeseed along with any customs reductions to enable domestic producers to recover after two bad seasons in a row.
"We expect rapeseed output to amount to about 400,000 to 450,000 tonnes, with production meeting about 40 to 45 percent of demand from domestic edible oil processing plants," he said.
"There are proposals to lower rapeseed duties...but we must be very cautious, and look in the longer-term, in order to rebuild domestic production," Kalinowski said.
Customs duties on rapeseed now amount to three (corrects from "four") percent.
According to the Central Statistical Office (GUS) about 50 percent of winter rapeseed crops were destroyed over the cold and relatively snow-free winter.
